name: The Bald Cypresses of Parco Marenzi
verified_sources: data/registers/italy-masaf.json (sheets 06/A794/BG/03, girth 455cm/32m, and 07/A794/BG/03, girth 380cm/33m, both Parco Marenzi, Bergamo; a third sheet 05/A794/BG/03 registers the pair again as an 'insieme omogeneo', same coordinates, folded here rather than shipped separately)

https://www.bergamonews.it/2025/05/08/alla-scoperta-dei-cipressi-monumentali-del-parco-marenzi-visita-guidata-ed-esperienza-di-forest-bathing/801068/ (8 May 2025: guided nature walk among the park's bald cypresses, 'over two centuries of life', roughly 35m tall)

https://primabergamo.it/ambiente/finalmente-riaperto-e-risplende-il-parco-marenzi-di-bergamo-un-santuario-per-la-biodiversita-urbana/ (20 April 2026: park reopened to the public after restoration of its historic pond, names 'two imposing bald cypresses over 25m tall' among the park's monumental trees)
access: Free, public municipal park, reopened 20 April 2026 after pond restoration.
transport: Central Bergamo (Citta Bassa), about a 10 to 15 minute walk from Porta Nuova.
verify_notes: Two mature bald cypresses (a native of American swamps, rare in an Italian urban park) stand by the park's small artificial lake, the tallest with a trunk over 4m round. Register gives 455cm/32m and 380cm/33m for the two named specimens; a third register sheet groups them again as a homogeneous pair at the same coordinates, so treat as one destination rather than three register lines. Bergamonews (8 May 2025) ran a guided 'forest bathing' walk here for the National Day of Monumental Trees, calling them 'over two centuries' old and noting bald cypress can live to 1,000 years. Primabergamo (20 April 2026) confirms the park, a 9,000 sqm 19th-century garden 'like a secret garden behind walls', reopened to the public that day after a 180,000 euro restoration of the pond and its water system; both cypresses are named as still standing. Good remarkable-species angle: this is a swamp tree from the American South thriving in a Lombard city park, and its 'knees' (root growths) are visible at the pond's edge per the tourism copy.

name: The Giant Cedar of Pedrengo
verified_sources: data/registers/italy-masaf.json (sheet 01/G412/BG/03, girth 683cm, height 32m, Parco Frizzoni, Pedrengo)

https://www.in-lombardia.it/turismo-in-lombardia/bergamo-turismo/i-cedri-giganti-di-pedrengo (regional tourism board page: 35m tall, trunk circumference 7.20m / diameter 230cm, crown 25m wide, planted end of the 19th century, lightning-protection system installed on the trunk)
access: Free, small public urban park (Parco Frizzoni), a Fondo Ambiente Italiano (FAI) recognised site.
transport: Pedrengo, a village about 5km / roughly 15 minutes by car or local bus from central Bergamo; day-trip distance, not walkable from the city centre.
verify_notes: The single most spectacular tree in this batch: a Himalayan cedar standing alone at the centre of the lawn in a small public park, 683cm girth per the national register versus 720cm circumference per the regional tourism page (measurement variance, same tree, not a conflict worth hedging over since both describe an exceptional specimen); height given as 32m (register) or 35m (tourism page). Pyramidal crown with a distinctive drooping 'stork's nest' tip typical of very old deodara. Planted late 19th century per the tourism page (no precise year), giving a rough age of a century to a century and a half; age range here is inferred from 'planted end of the 19th century' rather than a direct age figure, so treat with the same caution as an estimate. Protected with a fenced root zone and a lightning-conductor on the trunk. A group of three more large cedars of the same species stands nearby in the same park, not separately registered. This is a day-trip addition (about 5km/15 minutes from Bergamo centre), not part of the walkable city-centre cluster; label honestly as Pedrengo, not Bergamo.
